data.one_liner: Ready-to-use micro-interactions and animations for Flutter, including AI interface motion.
data.what_it_does: Provides over 90 ready-to-use micro-interactions and animations, ranging from AI interface elements like thinking orbs and streaming text to text effects, custom borders, carousels, and controls. All widgets share core parameters like duration, curve, and enabled state, and respect platform accessibility settings.
use_when: You want to add professional UI micro-interactions or AI-themed interface elements to your Flutter app quickly.
You need ready-made animations like text reveals, custom glowing borders, or tilt cards without writing custom controllers.
avoid_when: You need a low-level framework for complex physics simulations or custom vector graphics animations where Rive or Lottie are a better fit.
Your project targets Flutter versions older than 3.44.
strengths: Simple API with sensible defaults that require minimal code.
Extensive collection of modern AI-specific UI widgets like thinking orbs, streaming text, and voice glows.
Built-in accessibility support for reduce motion settings, screen readers, and keyboard focus.
No extra dependencies outside of Flutter.
weaknesses: Requires a relatively recent minimum Flutter version (3.44 or newer).
Large widget collection increases the risk of inconsistent UI styles if not used carefully.

alternatives.name: flutter_animate
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose flutter_animate if you prefer a fluent extension-method approach to chain generic animations onto any Flutter widget.

alternatives.name: lottie
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose lottie if you want to use complex vector animations exported from After Effects instead of programmatic code-based micro-interactions.

alternatives.name: rive
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose rive if you need interactive, state-driven vector animations and animations controlled by state machines.
